sutta: 7.11. On one occasion, the Blessed One was dwelling among the Magadhans at Dakkhinagiri near the Brahmin village of Ekanala. Now, on that occasion, the Brahmin Kasi Bharadvaja Bharadvaja the Plowman had 500 plows fastened to their yokes at the time of sowing. Then in the morning, the Blessed One dressed and taking bowl and robe went to the place where the Brahmin Kasi Bharadvaja was at work. Now, on that occasion, the Brahmin Kasi Bharadvaja's food distribution was taking place. Then the Blessed One approached the place of the food distribution and stood to one side. The Brahmin Kasi Bharadvaja saw the Blessed One standing for alms and said to him, "Recluse, I plow and sow, and when I have plowed and sown, I eat. You too, ascetic, ought to plow and sow. Then when you have plowed and sown, you will eat." Let's stop here for a moment. So, this uh Brahmin now must have been a rich man. He got 500 flowers already to work to sow seeds and all that. So, all his workers must have been standing ready to work. So, he was full time. So, the Buddha came to ask for alms. Then, he thought the Buddha like a lot of people think that monks are lazy people, only beg for their food, and then go and sleep. So, he told the Buddha, "We have to work for our food. You also ought to work for your food." And the Buddha said, "I too, Brahmin, plow and sow. And when I have plowed and sown, I eat." And he said, "But we do not see Master Gotama's yoke or plow or plowshare or goad or oxen. Yet Master Gotama says, 'I too, Brahmin, plow and sow. And when I have plowed and sown, I eat.'" Then the Brahmin Kasi Bharadvaja addressed the Blessed One in verse, "You claim to be a man who works the plow. I do not see your plowing. If you are a plowman, answer me, how should we understand your plowing?" And the Buddha said, "Faith is the seed, austerity the rain, wisdom my yoke and plow, shame the pole, mind the yoke tie, mindfulness my plowshare and goad, guarded in body, guarded in speech, controlled in my appetite for food. I use truth as my weeding hook and gentleness as my unyoking. Energy is my beast of burden, carrying me to security from bondage. It goes ahead without stopping to where, having gone, one does not sorrow. In such a way this plowing is done, which has the deathless as its fruit." "Having finished this work of plowing, one is relieved from all suffering." And he said, "Let Master Gotama eat. The worthy is a plowman. Since Master Gotama does plowing that has even the deathless as its food. And the Buddha said, "Food over which verses have been sung is not fit to be eaten by the Buddha and all that." And this was said, the Brahmin to sin, Master Gotama. Frankly to sin, Master Gotama. The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama. As though he were turning upright what had been turned upside down, revealing what was hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, or holding up a lamp in the dark for those with eyesight to see forms. I go for refuge to Master Gotama and to the Dhamma and to Bhikkhu Sangha. Let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who from today has gone for refuge for life." So in the end he realized that the Buddha also works uh uh in a different way, works to attain the deathless. He was impressed, so he became a follower of the Buddha. But you see here he didn't ask to go forth and become a monk. Probably because he was a very rich man.
